# Spin

**Motion › Spin** · v1.0.0 · 36 frames at 30 fps (18–72)

A shape in the new background colour spins in at the centre and grows while the camera rolls with it, until it fills the frame; the new scene then spins into place.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/spin@1.0.0.mp4)

## Where it is used

- Playful scene changes
- Social and music content
- Retro TV looks

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import spin from './transitions/05-motion/spin/spin';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(spin, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 36 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#FF4F1A"` |  | The incoming scene's background colour; the transition brings it in. |
| `shape` | enum | `"square"` | `square` · `circle` | Shape that spins in. |
| `turns` | number | `0.5` | 0.1–2 | Turns the shape makes while it grows. |
| `roll` | number | `18` | 0–90 | Degrees the camera rolls along with it. |
| `counterClockwise` | boolean | `false` |  | Spin the other way. |
| `blur` | number | `8` | 0–30 | Peak motion blur in pixels. |
